places.name: Glendalough Spinc Trail
places.kicker: A high trail above two glacial lakes
places.description: Climb through the pine forest to a sweeping boardwalk over the Spinc ridge, with the Upper Lake opening below you and the Wicklow Mountains beyond.
places.address: Upper Lake Car Park, Glendalough, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Paid parking at the Upper Lake. Arrive before 10am on bright weekends.

places.name: Dunluce Castle
places.kicker: A cliff-edge castle with a wild history
places.description: Cross the narrow bridge to the dramatic ruins of Dunluce, perched above Atlantic caves and the Causeway Coast.
places.address: 87 Dunluce Road, Bushmills, BT57 8UY
places.parking: Small free car park beside the visitor centre.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher
places.kicker: Ireland’s most famous Atlantic edge
places.description: Walk the clifftop path as dark shale walls rise over the Atlantic. On a clear day, the Aran Islands sit low on the horizon.
places.address: Cliffs of Moher, Liscannor, Co. Clare, V95 KN9T
places.parking: Main visitor-centre parking includes admission. Book online for quieter times.

places.name: Inch Beach
places.kicker: A long golden strand on the Dingle peninsula
places.description: Walk, swim or watch surfers from this broad sandy spit with mountain views in almost every direction.
places.address: Inch, Co. Kerry
places.parking: Park on the firm section of beach near the entrance; mind tide times.

places.name: Glenveagh National Park
places.kicker: Lakeside trails in Donegal’s mountain heart
places.description: Follow the valley road beside Lough Veagh to the castle gardens, surrounded by rugged Derryveagh peaks.
places.address: Church Hill, Letterkenny, Co. Donegal, F92 P993
places.parking: Free visitor-centre car park. Shuttle to the castle runs seasonally.

places.name: Slieve League
places.kicker: Immense sea cliffs at the edge of Europe
places.description: A steep coastal viewpoint where the Donegal mountains fall straight into the Atlantic. The upper path is for confident walkers only.
places.address: Bunglas Road, Teelin, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Lower car park with seasonal shuttle; limited access higher up.

places.name: Rock of Cashel
places.kicker: A limestone crown above the Golden Vale
places.description: Explore a remarkable collection of medieval buildings gathered on a dramatic outcrop above Cashel town.
places.address: St. Patrick’s Rock, Cashel, Co. Tipperary
places.parking: Paid public parking in Cashel, a short uphill walk away.

places.name: Giant’s Causeway
places.kicker: 40,000 basalt columns on the Causeway Coast
places.description: Walk out onto the hexagonal stones formed by an ancient volcanic eruption, with myth attributing them to the giant Finn McCool. The clifftop path gives free access to the stones without going through the visitor centre.
places.address: Giant’s Causeway, Bushmills, Co. Antrim, BT57 8SU
places.parking: Paid National Trust visitor-centre parking; free roadside and clifftop-path alternatives nearby.

places.name: Poulnabrone Dolmen
places.kicker: A 5,000-year-old portal tomb on the Burren’s limestone pavement
places.description: One of Ireland’s oldest and most photographed monuments, standing alone on exposed karst limestone. Excavations found the remains of over 30 people beneath the capstone.
places.address: Poulnabrone, Co. Clare
places.parking: Free roadside car park on the R480.

places.name: Mussenden Temple & Downhill Demesne
places.cost: Free (paid NT parking, or free at Bishop’s Gate)
places.kicker: A cliff-edge library modelled on an Italian temple
places.description: This 18th-century rotunda, built as a library for an eccentric bishop, sits close enough to the cliff edge that it looks ready to fall in. The demesne’s ruined mansion and gardens spread out behind it above the Atlantic.
places.address: Downhill Demesne, Mussenden Road, Castlerock, Co. Derry~Londonderry, BT51 4RP
places.parking: National Trust car park charges a fee; free parking further along the A2 at Bishop’s Gate.

places.name: Keem Bay
places.cost: Free (pay & display fills early in summer)
places.kicker: Ireland’s most-loved beach, ringed by cliffs
places.description: A horseshoe of white sand at the western tip of Achill Island, hemmed in by steep green cliffs on three sides and the open Atlantic on the fourth. Regularly voted Ireland’s best beach.
places.address: Keem Bay, Achill Island, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Car park above the beach; arrive before 11am on summer days.

places.name: Dog’s Bay & Gurteen Bay
places.kicker: A tombolo of two white shell-sand beaches
places.description: Back-to-back beaches joined by a narrow spit near Roundstone, with turquoise water and sand made almost entirely of tiny fossilised shells. One of Connemara’s most striking coastal walks.
places.address: Dog’s Bay, Roundstone, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free car parking behind both beaches.

places.name: Cobh Waterfront & Titanic Memorial
places.kicker: The Titanic’s last port of call
places.description: Walk the pastel harbour-front promenade where 123 passengers boarded the Titanic in 1912, its final stop before the Atlantic. The Lusitania Peace Memorial and cathedral views add to a town built on emigration history.
places.address: Cobh Promenade, Co. Cork
places.parking: Free on-street parking around the town; paid car parks near the seafront.

places.name: Slieve Gullion Passage Tomb
places.distance: 1.5 km return from top car park
places.kicker: The highest surviving passage tomb in Ireland or Britain
places.description: Climb from the forest-drive car park to the Neolithic South Cairn on Armagh’s highest summit, with a small lake in the crater behind it and panoramic views over the Ring of Gullion.
places.address: Slieve Gullion Forest Park, Newry Road, Co. Armagh
places.parking: Free car park at the top of the scenic forest drive.

places.name: Trinity College Campus
places.kicker: Ireland’s oldest university, in the heart of the city
places.description: Wander cobbled squares dating to 1592, past the Campanile and the Rubrics to the Old Library building. The Long Room and Book of Kells need a ticket; the campus itself doesn’t.
places.address: Trinity College, College Green, Dublin 2
places.parking: No on-site parking; use city-centre paid car parks or public transport.

places.name: Benbulben View at Drumcliffe
places.kicker: Yeats country, under Ireland’s iconic table mountain
places.description: Visit W.B. Yeats’s grave in Drumcliffe churchyard with Benbulben’s flat-topped silhouette rising behind it, the view that shaped his best-known epitaph.
places.address: Drumcliffe Church, Co. Sligo
places.parking: Free car park at the church.

places.name: Hill of Tara
places.kicker: The ancient seat of Ireland’s High Kings
places.description: Walk the open grassy mounds of a royal and ceremonial site used for over 5,000 years, including the Stone of Destiny where High Kings were once crowned, with views across the Boyne Valley.
places.address: Hill of Tara, Co. Meath
places.parking: Free car park at the visitor centre.

places.name: Glenbarrow Waterfall Loop
places.kicker: A three-tiered waterfall hidden in the Slieve Bloom Mountains
places.description: Follow the River Barrow upstream through mature conifer woodland to Clamp Hole, where the water tumbles over three rocky tiers. The midlands hide some of Ireland’s quietest walking country, and this loop rarely sees a queue.
places.address: Glenbarrow car park, Rosenallis, Co. Laois
places.parking: Free car park at the trailhead, signposted from Rosenallis village.

places.name: Magho Viewpoint, Lough Navar Forest
places.kicker: A 300m clifftop panorama over Lower Lough Erne
places.description: Drive the Lough Navar Forest Drive to its highest point for a sweeping view across the lough’s scattered islands, stretching into Donegal, Sligo and Tyrone on a clear day.
places.address: Lough Navar Forest, Derrygonnelly, Co. Fermanagh
places.parking: Free car park at the viewpoint, reached via the forest drive.

places.name: Lough Boora Discovery Park
places.kicker: A reclaimed bogland trail strung with large-scale sculpture
places.description: Follow the sculpture loop across former industrial cutaway bog, now a wetland sanctuary, passing two dozen artworks built from rail line, timber and stone.
places.address: Lough Boora Discovery Park, Kilcormac, Co. Offaly
places.parking: Free car park, open 8am-6pm year-round.

places.name: Clare Glens
places.kicker: A red sandstone gorge of cascading waterfalls
places.description: Cross footbridges through mixed woodland as the Clare River drops through a series of falls on the Limerick-Tipperary border, one of the midlands’ best-kept walking secrets.
places.address: Clare Glens car park, Murroe, Co. Limerick
places.parking: Free roadside car park beside the bridge, signposted from Murroe and Newport.

places.name: Murlough Beach
places.kicker: Four miles of dune-backed strand beneath the Mournes
places.description: Boardwalks cross a 6,000-year-old dune system to a long golden beach with the Mourne Mountains rising behind it, one of the finest coastal nature reserves in the north.
places.address: Murlough National Nature Reserve, Dundrum, Co. Down
places.parking: National Trust car park, seasonal charge (roughly £3-£7); free for NT members.

places.name: Cavan Burren Park
places.kicker: A megalithic landscape of tombs and pre-bog walls
places.description: Wander a small, spiritual landscape of wedge and portal tombs, hut sites and stone-age field walls, overlooked by Cuilcagh Mountain, then follow the Cavan Way onward to the Shannon Pot, source of Ireland’s longest river.
places.address: Cavan Burren Park, Blacklion, Co. Cavan
places.parking: Free car park with interpretive centre and picnic area.

places.name: Slieve Foye & Carlingford Lough Loop
places.kicker: A mountain loop above Ireland’s fjord-like lough
places.description: Climb from the medieval streets of Carlingford through forestry and open mountain to the 589m summit of Slieve Foye, with the lough, the Mournes and the Cooley Peninsula spread out below.
places.address: Carlingford Tourist Office car park, Co. Louth
places.parking: Free car parking beside the harbour in Carlingford.

places.name: Davagh Forest (OM Dark Sky Park)
places.kicker: Stargazing and a Bronze Age stone circle complex
places.description: One of Ireland’s few designated Dark Sky Parks, in the foothills of the Sperrins. Follow the Solar Walk boardwalk from the observatory out to the Beaghmore Stone Circles, laid out by astronomers 4,000 years before this one existed.
places.address: Davagh Forest, Cookstown, Co. Tyrone
places.parking: Free car parks (upper and lower) on site.

places.name: Ballinesker Beach, Curracloe
places.kicker: An eight-mile strand that stood in for Normandy
places.description: Steven Spielberg filmed the D-Day landing scenes of Saving Private Ryan on this vast stretch of dune-backed sand. On an ordinary day it’s simply one of the east coast’s best beaches for a long walk.
places.address: Curracloe Beach, Co. Wexford
places.parking: Free car parks at Ballinesker, White Gap and Culletons Gap.

places.name: Woodstock Gardens & Forest Park
places.cost: Free (small car-park charge near the gardens)
places.kicker: Victorian gardens and an ivy-covered avenue above the Nore
places.description: Wander terraced gardens, a noble fir avenue and woodland walks above the ruins of Woodstock House, with the River Nore and Inistioge village below.
places.address: Woodstock Gardens, Inistioge, Co. Kilkenny
places.parking: Small free car park near the village bridge; paid car park at the main gardens entrance.

places.name: Brownshill Dolmen
places.kicker: Europe’s heaviest capstone, balanced for 5,000 years
places.description: Stand beneath the largest known capstone of any dolmen in Europe, an estimated 100+ tonne slab of granite resting on three uprights just outside Carlow town.
places.address: Brownshill Dolmen, Kernanstown, Co. Carlow
places.parking: Free car park at the site, signposted from Carlow town.

places.name: Altamont Gardens
places.kicker: A romantic garden above the River Slaney
places.description: Wander sweeping lawns, a spring-fed lake and an ancient oak wood at one of Ireland’s finest gardens, laid out over three generations and gifted to the state in 1999. Entry has always been free.
places.address: Altamont Gardens, Ballon, Co. Carlow, R93 W240
places.parking: Free car park at the visitor centre.

places.name: The Curragh Plains
places.kicker: A vast open common at the heart of Irish horse racing
places.description: Walk or picnic across nearly 5,000 acres of unfenced grassland, grazed since the Bronze Age and still home to racehorse strings on their morning gallops beside the racecourse.
places.address: The Curragh, Co. Kildare
places.parking: Free roadside parking around the plain.

places.name: Castletown House Parkland
places.kicker: Ireland’s grandest Palladian house, with free parkland to explore
places.description: Walk the tree-lined avenue and riverside paths of Ireland’s largest and earliest Palladian house, past follies and the Liffey — the guided house tour is the only part that costs anything.
places.address: Castletown House, Celbridge, Co. Kildare, W23 RP62
places.parking: Free car park on site.

places.name: Glencar Waterfall
places.kicker: The waterfall Yeats made famous in verse
places.description: A short path leads to a 15-metre cascade tumbling into wooded Glencar Lake, the setting for W.B. Yeats’s poem “The Stolen Child” and one of the northwest’s easiest big-view walks.
places.address: Glencar Waterfall, Co. Leitrim
places.parking: Free car park at the trailhead on the R284.

places.name: Lough Rynn Estate
places.kicker: A lakeside demesne once home to the Earls of Leitrim
places.description: Follow woodland and lakeshore trails through a 300-year-old estate, past a ruined castle, walled garden and Lough Rynn itself, with a mile-long lakeside walk that rarely feels busy.
places.address: Lough Rynn Estate, Mohill, Co. Leitrim, N41 KV81
places.parking: Free car park at the estate entrance.

places.name: Royal Canal Greenway – Richmond Harbour
places.kicker: A traffic-free towpath where the Royal Canal meets the Shannon
places.description: Walk or cycle the flat towpath where the 145 km Royal Canal Greenway reaches its western end at a quiet stone harbour, with locks, an old dry dock and swans for company.
places.address: Richmond Harbour, Cloondara, Co. Longford
places.parking: Free car park at the harbour.

places.name: Ardagh Heritage Village
places.kicker: A tidy Victorian estate village frozen in time
places.description: Wander a picture-book cluster of thatched and slated cottages built around a green by the Fetherston family in the 1860s, with a small heritage centre and holy well a short walk beyond.
places.address: Ardagh, Co. Longford
places.parking: Free parking on the village green.

places.name: Rossmore Forest Park
places.kicker: Lakeside forest trails around a ruined Victorian castle
places.description: Follow waymarked trails through mixed woodland and past several small lakes to the ruins of Rossmore Castle, once one of Ulster’s grandest houses.
places.address: Rossmore Forest Park, Monaghan, Co. Monaghan
places.parking: Free car park at the entrance.

places.name: Monaghan County Museum
places.kicker: An award-winning free museum, now on the new Peace Campus
places.description: See the 14th-century Cross of Clogher and centuries of local history in a museum that has twice won the Council of Europe Museum Prize, all at no charge. It moved from Hill Street to the new Monaghan Peace Campus in 2024.
places.address: Monaghan Peace Campus, Plantation Road, Monaghan, Co. Monaghan, H18 RP20
places.parking: Free car parking at the Peace Campus.

places.name: Lough Key Forest Park
places.kicker: Island-dotted lake trails around a fairytale forest park
places.description: Wander lakeshore and woodland trails past follies, a moon gate and an underground tunnel network to views over island-studded Lough Key; the treetop canopy walk and boat trips cost extra, but the park itself is free.
places.address: Lough Key Forest Park, Boyle, Co. Roscommon
places.parking: Paid car park (small daily charge).

places.name: Rathcroghan (Cruachan Aí)
places.kicker: Connacht’s royal capital and the mythical home of Queen Maeve
places.description: Walk between more than 240 archaeological monuments scattered across open farmland, the ceremonial capital of Connacht for over 4,000 years and the legendary seat of Queen Maeve. The fields are free to explore, though the exhibition centre in the village charges.
places.address: Rathcroghan, Tulsk, Co. Roscommon
places.parking: Free roadside parking near the monuments.

places.name: Mahon Falls
places.kicker: A dramatic cascade at the head of a glacial valley
places.description: Follow a rough path up a U-shaped glacial valley in the Comeraghs to where the Mahon River drops over a rock face, one of the most photographed short walks in the southeast.
places.address: Mahon Falls, Comeragh Mountains, Co. Waterford
places.parking: Free car park at the trailhead.

places.name: Waterford Greenway
places.kicker: Ireland’s longest off-road greenway, on an old railway line
places.description: Walk or cycle a flat, fully off-road former railway line from Waterford city to Dungarvan, crossing viaducts and the 400 m Ballyvoyle Tunnel with sea views along the final stretch.
places.address: Waterford Greenway, Kilmeaden, Co. Waterford
places.parking: Free car parks at multiple access points along the route.

places.name: Hill of Uisneach
places.cost: Free to view from the road; guided hilltop walk ~€16pp (seasonal, pre-booked)
places.kicker: The mythical centre of Ireland
places.description: The broad hill said to be the ceremonial and spiritual centre of ancient Ireland, topped by the Cat Stone marking the meeting point of the five provinces, sits on private working farmland. It’s visible and free from the surrounding road, but reaching the summit means joining a seasonal, pre-booked guided walk.
places.address: Hill of Uisneach, Ballymore, Co. Westmeath
places.parking: Parking provided as part of the guided-walk booking.

places.name: Fore Abbey & the Seven Wonders of Fore
places.kicker: A ruined Benedictine abbey and its seven medieval “wonders”
places.description: Explore the ruins of a 7th-century monastic site tucked into a quiet valley, still associated with seven local “wonders” including a mill without a stream and a tree said never to burn.
places.address: Fore Abbey, Fore, Co. Westmeath
places.parking: Free car park in the village.

places.name: Torc Waterfall
places.cost: Free (paid car park at the base)
places.kicker: Killarney National Park’s most-photographed waterfall
places.description: Climb a short path to where the Owengarriff River drops 20 metres through mossy woodland, then continue up the Old Kenmare Road for views over the Killarney lakes — inside a national park that never charges for entry.
places.address: Torc Waterfall, Killarney National Park, Co. Kerry
places.parking: Paid car park at the trailhead on the N71.

places.name: Phoenix Park
places.kicker: One of Europe’s largest enclosed city parks
places.description: Roam 700 hectares of parkland minutes from the city centre, home to a wild fallow deer herd, the Wellington Monument and the President’s residence, with free walking and cycling trails throughout.
places.address: Phoenix Park, Dublin 8
places.parking: Free car parking within the park.

places.name: Diamond Hill, Connemara National Park
places.kicker: A quartzite peak with the best view in Connemara
places.description: Climb a boardwalked and stepped trail through bogland and heath to the 442 m summit of Diamond Hill, with the Twelve Bens, Kylemore Abbey and the Atlantic all visible from the top. Entry to the national park is free.
places.address: Connemara National Park, Letterfrack, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free car park at the visitor centre.

places.name: Gougane Barra
places.cost: Free (€5 forest park car park charge)
places.kicker: A hidden lake where the River Lee begins
places.description: Walk the forested shore of a mountain-ringed lake to St Finbarr’s tiny oratory on its own island, connected by a causeway — the spot where Cork’s patron saint founded a monastery, and where the River Lee rises.
places.address: Gougane Barra, Ballingeary, Co. Cork
places.parking: Coillte forest park car park, €5 charge.

places.name: Croagh Patrick
places.kicker: Ireland’s holy mountain, climbed by pilgrims for 1,500 years
places.description: Climb the scree-topped cone above Clew Bay on the same path pilgrims have walked (some barefoot) since St Patrick’s 40-day fast here in 441 AD, with the bay’s scattered “drowned drumlin” islands opening out below.
places.address: Murrisk, near Westport, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Free car park at Murrisk, at the foot of the mountain.

places.name: Downpatrick Head
places.kicker: A clifftop blowhole beside the sea stack of Dún Briste
places.description: Walk the open clifftop to Dún Briste, a 45m sea stack that sheared from the mainland in a 1393 storm, marooning a family who were rescued the next day, plus a roaring blowhole underfoot — mind the unfenced edges.
places.address: Ballycastle, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Free car park at the site, 6 km north of Ballycastle village.

places.name: Malin Head
places.kicker: The most northerly point on mainland Ireland
places.description: Walk the headland to Banba’s Crown, an 1805 signal tower, past the huge “EIRE 80” marker cut into the cliff to warn WWII pilots of neutral ground, with Inishowen’s Atlantic edge stretching out on every side.
places.address: Banba’s Crown, Malin Head, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Free car park at Banba’s Crown.

places.name: Fanad Head Lighthouse
places.kicker: Regularly voted one of the most beautiful lighthouses in the world
places.description: First lit on St Patrick’s Day 1817 after the wreck of HMS Saldanha claimed 250 lives nearby. The grounds and headland views are free; climbing the 76-step tower is a paid tour.
places.address: Fanad Head, near Portsalon, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Free car park at the lighthouse.
facts: One of the world’s prettiest lighthouses

places.name: Mount Errigal
places.kicker: Donegal’s highest peak, glowing pink at sunset
places.description: Climb the quartzite scree of Errigal’s near-perfect cone, the highest of the Derryveagh range’s “Seven Sisters”, for a summit view across Donegal’s loughs and coastline that has been called Ireland’s answer to Fuji.
places.address: R251 car park, near Dunlewey/Gweedore, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Free roadside car park on the R251.

places.name: Fair Head
places.kicker: Ireland’s biggest cliff face, a dolerite wall popular with rock climbers
places.description: Walk the plateau above a 100m-plus sheer dolerite cliff formed 60 million years ago, past the Lough na Cranagh crannóg, with views to Rathlin Island and Scotland’s Mull of Kintyre on a clear day.
places.address: Coolanlough Road, near Ballycastle, Co. Antrim
places.parking: Small seasonal car-park charge at Ballyvoy/Coolanlough Road.

places.name: Dark Hedges
places.kicker: A beech-tree tunnel made famous as Game of Thrones’ Kingsroad
places.description: Walk the gnarled avenue of beech trees planted by the Stuart family around 1775 as the entrance to Gracehill House, fewer than 90 of the original ~150 now standing, still one of the most photographed roads in Ireland.
places.address: Bregagh Road, Stranocum, Ballymoney, Co. Antrim, BT53 8PX
places.parking: Small pay-and-display car park nearby; road itself is public.

places.name: Giant’s Ring
places.kicker: A 5,000-year-old Neolithic henge on Belfast’s edge
places.description: Walk the perimeter of a huge circular earthwork bank, 180m across and up to 3.5m high, enclosing a central passage-tomb dolmen dating to around 3000 BC — open access with no ticket booth.
places.address: Off Ballynahatty Road, near Shaw’s Bridge, Belfast, Co. Down
places.parking: Park at Minnowburn/Shaw’s Bridge and walk across the field.

places.name: Cave Hill Country Park
places.kicker: Belfast’s basalt hilltop, said to have inspired Gulliver’s Travels
places.description: Climb to McArt’s Fort, an ancient promontory fort atop the cliff profile nicknamed “Napoleon’s Nose”, where Wolfe Tone and the United Irishmen are said to have met in 1795, with the whole of Belfast and Belfast Lough spread out below.
places.address: Belfast Castle car park, Antrim Road, Belfast, BT15 5GR
places.parking: Free car park at Belfast Castle.

places.name: Divis and the Black Mountain
places.kicker: A former army lookout turned open moorland above Belfast
places.description: Walk open heather moorland to Divis’s 478m summit trig point, past the site of a WWII plane-crash memorial on ground once used by the British Army, for panoramic views over Belfast and Belfast Lough.
places.address: Divis Road, Upper Springfield Road, Belfast, Co. Antrim
places.parking: Free National Trust car park (café/upper car park closed for construction until spring 2027).

places.name: Portstewart Strand
places.cost: Free (paid NT car park for non-members)
places.kicker: A two-mile Blue Flag beach where you can still drive onto the sand
places.description: Walk a broad strand backed by 6,000-year-old dunes up to 30m high, one of the few Irish beaches where cars are still permitted onto the sand, and the starting point of the 33-mile Causeway Coast Way.
places.address: Strand Road, Portstewart, Co. Derry~Londonderry
places.parking: National Trust car park; free for members, paid for non-members.

places.name: Whitepark Bay
places.kicker: A secluded, mile-wide sandy bay far quieter than the Causeway crowds
places.description: Walk a broad National Trust beach backed by ancient dunes home to at least nine orchid species, with fossils regularly exposed in cliff landslips — beautiful, but unsuitable for swimming due to rip currents.
places.address: Off the B15/A2 coast road, near Ballintoy, Co. Antrim
places.parking: Free National Trust car park.

places.name: Ballintoy Harbour
places.kicker: A tiny working harbour that played the Iron Islands’ port of Pyke in Game of Thrones
places.description: A tiny working harbour with whitewashed limestone walls set against dark basalt cliffs, made famous by its Game of Thrones appearances.
places.address: Harbour Road, Ballintoy, Ballycastle, Co. Antrim, BT54 6NA
places.parking: Small pay car park above the harbour.

places.name: Slemish Mountain
places.kicker: The volcanic plug where St Patrick is said to have herded sheep
places.description: Climb the eroded core of an extinct volcano where tradition holds a young, enslaved St Patrick tended sheep for six years — still Antrim’s biggest gathering point every St Patrick’s Day.
places.address: Slemish car park, near Broughshane, Co. Antrim
places.parking: Free car park at the trailhead (toilets on site).

places.name: Killiney Hill Park
places.kicker: Dublin’s “Bay of Naples” view over Killiney Bay
places.description: Walk looped paths through gorse and woodland to an 1742 famine-relief obelisk at the summit, with sweeping views over Killiney Bay to the Wicklow Mountains that have long earned the area its “Bay of Naples” nickname.
places.address: Victoria/Killiney Hill car park, off Vico Road, Dublin
places.parking: Free car park off Vico Road/Dalkey Avenue.

places.name: Howth Cliff Walk
places.kicker: A clifftop loop above Dublin Bay, easily reached by DART
places.description: Follow the clifftop path around Howth Head past the 1814 Baily Lighthouse, with views to Ireland’s Eye, Lambay Island and, on a clear day, Wales — one of Dublin’s most popular free walks, right at the end of the DART line.
places.address: Howth village or Summit car park, Howth, Dublin
places.parking: Free car parking near Howth village and at the Summit.

places.name: Bray to Greystones Cliff Walk
places.kicker: A railway-side clifftop path between two seaside towns
places.description: Follow a path cut by 1840s railway workers along the cliffs between Bray and Greystones, with views to the Sugar Loaf and the Irish Sea; sections have closed intermittently after landslides, so check local conditions before setting out.
places.address: Bray seafront (bandstand), Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Free on-street and seafront parking in Bray.
facts: Cut by rail workers in the 1840s

places.name: Lough Tay (Guinness Lake), Sally Gap
places.kicker: A jet-black lake with a white sand beach that looks like a poured pint of stout
places.description: Stop at the roadside viewpoints above Lough Tay, framed by the cliffs of Luggala, where the Guinness family estate’s imported white sand completes the illusion — the lake shore itself is private, but the view from the R759 is free and unforgettable.
places.address: R759, near Sally Gap, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Free roadside car parks (J.B. Malone / Ballinastoe Wood) on the R759.
facts: View only, lake shore is private

places.name: Glendalough Monastic City
places.kicker: A 6th-century monastic settlement, free to explore beside a paid exhibition
places.description: Wander the graveyard, cathedral ruins, St Kevin’s Church and 30m round tower of the monastery St Kevin founded around 570 AD — the site and grounds are free and open year-round, only the visitor-centre exhibition next door charges.
places.address: Glendalough Visitor Centre, near Laragh, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Paid car park at the visitor centre; site access itself is free.

places.name: Sky Road, Clifden
places.kicker: A cliff-top loop road around Connemara’s most dramatic coastline
places.description: Drive or walk the loop around the Kingston peninsula past the ruins of Clifden Castle (c. 1818) and the monument to town founder John D’Arcy, with the Atlantic and Connemara’s islands opening out from the high point.
places.address: Clifden town, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free car park at the loop’s highest point; roadside parking elsewhere.

places.name: Coole Park
places.kicker: Lady Gregory’s estate, where Yeats carved his initials into a tree
places.description: Walk looped nature trails to the “Autograph Tree”, a copper beech carved with the initials of W.B. Yeats (1898), G.B. Shaw, J.M. Synge and other figures of the Irish Literary Revival who gathered here, the setting for Yeats’s “The Wild Swans at Coole”.
places.address: Coole Park, off the N18, near Gort, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free car park at the visitor centre.

places.name: Athenry Town Walls
places.kicker: Ireland’s best-preserved medieval town walls
places.description: Walk sections of the 13th-century walls raised under an 1310 murage grant, roughly 70% of the original circuit still standing around an almost untouched medieval street plan — the walls and streets are free, only the separate castle charges admission.
places.address: Athenry town centre, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free on-street parking in Athenry.

places.name: Lough Gur
places.kicker: Ireland’s largest stone circle beside a lake settled for 6,000 years
places.description: Walk to the Grange Stone Circle, 113 standing stones aligned to the summer solstice sunrise, then follow the horseshoe-shaped lake past wedge tombs and early Christian remains — the stone circle and lakeshore are free, the visitor centre exhibition is not.
places.address: Grange Stone Circle, near Bruff/Holycross, Co. Limerick
places.parking: Free car park at the stone circle; paid parking at the visitor centre.

places.name: Kilkee Cliff Walk
places.kicker: A quieter answer to the Cliffs of Moher, on the Loop Head Peninsula
places.description: Follow the loop around Kilkee’s Duggerna Reef and West End cliffs, unfenced Atlantic drama without the Cliffs of Moher crowds, on the same Loop Head Peninsula as the 1854 lighthouse further west.
places.address: Kilkee town/West End, Co. Clare
places.parking: Free on-street parking in Kilkee.

places.name: The Vee
places.kicker: A hairpin mountain pass with a chevron-shaped view over the Golden Vale
places.description: Stop at the V-shaped bend on the old Lismore-Clogheen coach road through the Knockmealdowns, past a famine-era memorial cairn, for a sweeping view over the Golden Vale — spectacular when the rhododendrons bloom in late May.
places.address: R668, between Clogheen, Co. Tipperary and Lismore, Co. Waterford
places.parking: Free car park at the viewpoint.

places.name: Carrauntoohil
places.kicker: Ireland’s highest summit above the MacGillycuddy’s Reeks
places.description: Follow the Hag’s Glen beneath steep mountain walls before the final climb to Ireland’s 1,039 m summit. This is a serious mountain day: cloud, wind and wet rock can change the character of the route quickly.
places.address: Cronin’s Yard, Mealis, Beaufort, Co. Kerry
places.parking: Paid parking and facilities at Cronin’s Yard; arrive early on fair-weather weekends.

places.name: Gap of Dunloe
places.kicker: A narrow mountain pass threaded between five dark lakes
places.description: Walk or cycle the old road as it winds between the MacGillycuddy’s Reeks and Purple Mountain, passing stone bridges, glacial lakes and some of Kerry’s grandest close-range mountain scenery.
places.address: Kate Kearney’s Cottage, Gap of Dunloe, Beaufort, Co. Kerry
places.parking: Limited parking near Kate Kearney’s Cottage; do not obstruct residents or jarvey access.

places.name: Slea Head
places.kicker: Atlantic cliffs at the far edge of the Dingle Peninsula
places.description: Look across to the Blasket Islands from a coast of sea cliffs, green headlands and stone-walled fields. The best experience comes from stopping at marked pull-ins and walking short sections away from the road.
places.address: Slea Head Drive, Dún Chaoin, Co. Kerry
places.parking: Use signed viewing areas only; roadside space is tight in summer.

places.name: Mizen Head
places.kicker: A dramatic signal station above Atlantic sea arches
places.description: Cross the arched footbridge to the old signal station on Ireland’s south-westerly edge. Clifftop paths reveal deep inlets, offshore rocks and the full force of the Atlantic below.
places.address: Mizen Head Visitor Centre, Goleen, Co. Cork
places.parking: Large visitor-centre car park; opening and admission vary seasonally.

places.name: Barleycove Beach
places.kicker: A broad dune-backed beach near Mizen Head
places.description: A floating footbridge crosses the tidal channel to pale sand and a protected dune system formed after the 1755 Lisbon earthquake. Low tide opens a generous sweep for walking.
places.address: Barleycove, Goleen, Co. Cork
places.parking: Public parking beside the access road; spaces fill quickly on warm days.

places.name: Ballyhoura Forest Trails
places.kicker: Forest walking and Ireland’s largest mountain-bike trail network
places.description: Choose a short nature trail or one of the purpose-built cycling loops climbing through Ballyhoura Forest. Upper sections are exposed, while the trailhead has toilets, showers and a bike wash.
places.address: Glenosheen Trailhead, Ardpatrick, Co. Limerick
places.parking: Barrier car park at the trailhead; the operator currently charges for parking.

places.name: Galtymore
places.kicker: The highest point of the Galtee Mountains
places.description: Climb from the Black Road to a broad summit with views across the Golden Vale. The upper mountain is open and boggy, with steep ground and little shelter when cloud comes down.
places.address: Black Road trailhead, Skeheenarinky, Co. Tipperary
places.parking: Small free trailhead car park; park considerately and leave gates clear.

places.name: Coumshingaun Lough
places.kicker: A glacial amphitheatre high in the Comeragh Mountains
places.description: Climb onto the rim above a dark corrie lake for one of Ireland’s most arresting mountain views. The full circuit is steep and exposed; the lower out-and-back still gives a fine view into the coum.
places.address: Kilclooney Wood car park, Comeragh Mountains, Co. Waterford
places.parking: Small free car park; overflow must not block the narrow road.

places.name: Tramore Beach
places.kicker: A long Atlantic strand beside Tramore’s promenade
places.description: Walk from the lively promenade towards the quieter dunes and tidal backstrand, with a wide horizon and dependable sea air. Swimming conditions can change, so follow local lifeguard guidance.
places.address: Tramore Promenade, Co. Waterford
places.parking: Several public car parks serve the promenade; some spaces may be pay and display.

places.name: Hook Head Lighthouse
places.kicker: One of the world’s oldest working lighthouses
places.description: Walk the limestone headland around the striped medieval tower, watching Atlantic swell break across the rocks. Guided tours climb inside the lighthouse; the surrounding coast remains the main spectacle.
places.address: Hook Lighthouse, Churchtown, Hook Head, Co. Wexford
places.parking: Free on-site visitor parking; check tour times before travelling.

places.name: Raven Point Nature Reserve
places.kicker: Pine woodland meeting the dunes of Curracloe
places.description: Follow sandy forest tracks through the Raven before returning along a vast strand. The reserve protects an important dune system, so stay on established paths and keep dogs under close control.
places.address: Raven Wood, Curracloe, Co. Wexford
places.parking: Use the public beach access car parks at Curracloe or Culleton’s Gap.

places.name: Brittas Bay
places.kicker: Wicklow’s sweeping dune-backed east-coast beach
places.description: A broad ribbon of sand runs below protected dunes, with room for long walks even on busy days. Boardwalks reduce erosion and give straightforward access from the main car parks.
places.address: Brittas Bay, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: North and south car parks may charge seasonally; roadside parking is restricted.

places.name: Djouce Mountain
places.kicker: A Wicklow summit above the dark waters of Lough Tay
places.description: Boardwalk and mountain path climb from the Sally Gap road to broad views over Lough Tay, Powerscourt and the Wicklow uplands. Conditions are exposed and the peat surface is fragile off trail.
places.address: JB Malone car park, Old Military Road, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Small free car park; alternative access from Ballinastoe is longer.

places.name: Avondale Forest Park
places.kicker: Mature woodland around the birthplace of Irish forestry
places.description: Walk beneath giant trees on riverside and estate trails surrounding Avondale House. The forest paths are independent of the ticketed house and treetop attraction.
places.address: Avondale Forest Park, Rathdrum, Co. Wicklow
places.parking: Large on-site car park; parking or attraction charges may apply.

places.name: Dollymount Strand
places.kicker: A wild-feeling city beach on North Bull Island
places.description: Walk a long sandy strand with Dublin Bay, Howth and the Poolbeg chimneys on the horizon. The island is an internationally important nature reserve, especially for wintering birds.
places.address: North Bull Island, Clontarf, Dublin 5
places.parking: Use designated island and causeway parking; restrictions change during busy periods.

places.name: Newgrange
places.kicker: A 5,000-year-old passage tomb aligned to the winter solstice
places.description: Enter the great kerbed mound as part of a guided Brú na Bóinne visit and see Neolithic art carved into its stones. Access is controlled from the visitor centre, not directly at the monument.
places.address: Brú na Bóinne Visitor Centre, Donore, Co. Meath
places.parking: Free visitor-centre parking; advance booking is strongly recommended.

places.name: Trim Castle
places.kicker: Ireland’s largest Anglo-Norman castle beside the Boyne
places.description: Walk around the massive curtain walls and along the river to see the fortress from every angle. A guided ticket gives access to the unusual cruciform keep.
places.address: Castle Street, Trim, Co. Meath
places.parking: Town car parks and limited on-street spaces nearby; check local restrictions.

places.name: Killykeen Forest Park
places.kicker: Woodland trails among the islands of Lough Oughter
places.description: Easy forest tracks thread between small lakes, mixed woodland and quiet picnic clearings on the Lough Oughter system. It is a gentle place for walking, cycling and watching the water.
places.address: Killykeen Forest Park, Killeshandra, Co. Cavan
places.parking: Free forest car parks; opening gates and access can vary.

places.name: Clonmacnoise
places.kicker: A monastic city beside a bend in the Shannon
places.description: Round towers, high crosses and roofless churches gather on open ground above the river. The setting makes the early medieval site feel connected to the old water routes that sustained it.
places.address: Clonmacnoise, Shannonbridge, Co. Offaly
places.parking: Free visitor parking included with site access; check seasonal opening.

places.name: Ridge of Capard
places.kicker: A boardwalk to wide views from the Slieve Blooms
places.description: A short woodland climb and boardwalk lead to a high open ridge overlooking the central plain. On a clear day the view reaches far beyond Laois across Ireland’s midlands.
places.address: Ridge of Capard car park, Slieve Bloom Mountains, Co. Laois
places.parking: Free forest car park at the trailhead.

places.name: Kilkenny Castle Park
places.kicker: A riverside castle and open park in the heart of Kilkenny
places.description: Approach the great stone façade across sweeping lawns, then follow paths towards the River Nore. The park is free to roam while the restored castle rooms require admission.
places.address: The Parade, Kilkenny, Co. Kilkenny
places.parking: Use city-centre public car parks; the castle has no visitor parking.

places.name: Birr Castle Gardens
places.kicker: Historic gardens surrounding the Great Telescope
places.description: Explore mature woodland, formal terraces and lakes around a lived-in castle. The immense Leviathan telescope recalls the estate’s remarkable nineteenth-century scientific work.
places.address: Birr Castle Demesne, Birr, Co. Offaly
places.parking: Visitor parking near the main entrance; check opening dates and admission.

places.name: Portumna Forest Park
places.kicker: Lakeshore woodland beside Portumna Castle
places.description: Choose accessible forest paths or longer loops through old oak woodland to the shore of Lough Derg. Red squirrels and fallow deer reward a quiet pace.
places.address: Portumna Forest Park, Portumna, Co. Galway
places.parking: Free parking at the forest entrance and nearby harbour area.

places.name: Dún Aonghasa
places.kicker: A prehistoric stone fort poised above Atlantic cliffs
places.description: Climb across limestone pavement to concentric stone walls ending abruptly at a sheer cliff edge. There is no barrier at the cliff, and the exposed setting demands care in wind.
places.address: Kilmurvey, Inis Mór, Aran Islands, Co. Galway
places.parking: Leave bicycles at the visitor area; no private cars are needed on the approach.

places.name: Kylemore Abbey
places.kicker: A lakeside Victorian castle beneath Connemara mountains
places.description: The abbey’s pale façade reflects in Pollacapall Lough, backed by steep wooded slopes. Estate paths link the house, Gothic church and walled garden.
places.address: Kylemore Abbey, Connemara, Co. Galway
places.parking: Large free visitor car park; admission required beyond the entrance.

places.name: Mullaghmore Loop, Burren National Park
places.kicker: Terraced limestone and a wild Burren summit
places.description: A remote route crosses open limestone pavement beside Lough Gealáin before circling Mullaghmore. The rock is rough, waymarking can be subtle and there is little shelter.
places.address: Gortlecka trailhead, Burren National Park, Co. Clare
places.parking: Small free P1 car park at Gortlecka; never block the narrow road or gates.

places.name: Lahinch Beach
places.kicker: A broad surf beach facing the Atlantic
places.description: Walk the promenade and open sand with views south towards the Cliffs of Moher. Swell and currents can be powerful, making local safety advice essential for swimmers.
places.address: Lahinch Promenade, Co. Clare
places.parking: Town and promenade parking includes paid and time-limited spaces.

places.name: Enniscrone Beach
places.kicker: Golden sand and dunes at the mouth of Killala Bay
places.description: A long, open strand curves towards the Ox Mountains, giving ample room for walking and sea views. The dunes are protected, so use signed paths to reach the beach.
places.address: Enniscrone, Co. Sligo
places.parking: Public beach parking near the pier and main access points.

places.name: Knocknarea
places.kicker: Queen Maeve’s cairn above Sligo Bay
places.description: Climb through woodland and open mountain to a huge unopened passage-tomb cairn. Keep off the cairn itself and take in views over Strandhill, Benbulben and the Atlantic.
places.address: Queen Maeve Trail, Rathcarrick, Strandhill, Co. Sligo
places.parking: Dedicated trail car park; alternative access from Strandhill is longer.

places.name: Céide Fields
places.kicker: A Stone Age field system preserved beneath blanket bog
places.description: Boardwalks cross an exposed cliff-top landscape where stone walls lay hidden under peat for millennia. The visitor centre explains how farming communities shaped this coast more than 5,000 years ago.
places.address: Céide Fields, Ballycastle, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Free visitor-centre car park; check seasonal opening.

places.name: Wild Nephin National Park
places.kicker: Ireland’s largest roadless wilderness
places.description: Walk forest loops at Letterkeen or commit to remote mountain and bog routes beneath the Nephin Beg range. Longer journeys demand navigation, self-sufficiency and a reliable weather window.
places.address: Letterkeen trailhead, Newport, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Free trailhead parking; approach roads are narrow and remote.

places.name: Mulranny Beach
places.kicker: A sheltered strand overlooking the islands of Clew Bay
places.description: A causeway reaches sand, salt marsh and machair beneath the Nephin Beg mountains. The Great Western Greenway passes through the village just above the shore.
places.address: Mulranny Beach, Mulranny, Co. Mayo
places.parking: Free public car park near the causeway; spaces are limited in summer.

places.name: Silver Strand, Malin Beg
places.kicker: A horseshoe cove enclosed by high Donegal cliffs
places.description: From the viewing area, a steep staircase descends to pale sand and clear Atlantic water. The climb back is substantial, and tides can reduce the available beach.
places.address: Malin Beg, Glencolmcille, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Small free cliff-top car park; turning space is limited.

places.name: Ards Forest Park
places.cost: Free trails · parking charge may apply
places.kicker: Woodland, beaches and headlands around Sheephaven Bay
places.description: Marked trails move from deep forest to salt marsh, dunes and small sandy coves. Few Irish forest parks offer this much coastline within an easy network of loops.
places.address: Ards Forest Park, Creeslough, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Main forest car park at the N56 entrance; check current barrier charge.

places.name: Grianán of Aileach
places.kicker: An ancient ringfort commanding the Inishowen hills
places.description: Climb through thick circular walls to a parapet view across Lough Swilly, Lough Foyle and the surrounding counties. The exposed hilltop can be windy even on clear days.
places.address: Grianán of Aileach, Burt, Co. Donegal
places.parking: Free car park below the fort; final access road is narrow.

places.name: Marble Arch Caves
places.kicker: Underground rivers beneath the Cuilcagh landscape
places.description: A guided route enters a limestone world of chambers, pools and flowing water. Above ground, the free Cladagh Glen trail follows a wooded gorge towards the cave resurgence.
places.address: Marble Arch Caves, Florencecourt, Co. Fermanagh
places.parking: Free visitor parking; cave tours should be booked and can be affected by water levels.

places.name: Florence Court
places.kicker: An eighteenth-century house below Cuilcagh Mountain
places.description: Woodland and mountain-view trails spread around a grand National Trust house, kitchen garden and historic farmyard. The estate is also home to the original Irish yew.
places.address: Florence Court, Enniskillen, Co. Fermanagh, BT92 1DB
places.parking: National Trust car park; admission and parking arrangements vary by season.

places.name: Beaghmore Stone Circles
places.kicker: Bronze Age circles laid out beneath Sperrin skies
places.description: Boardwalks cross open bog to a complex of low stone circles, alignments and cairns. The isolated setting and broad sky are as memorable as the subtle archaeology.
places.address: Beaghmore Road, Cookstown, Co. Tyrone
places.parking: Free roadside car park beside the site.

places.name: Gortin Glen Forest Park
places.kicker: Sperrin woodland with a panoramic forest drive
places.description: Walk signed forest trails or follow the scenic drive to viewpoints over the Owenkillew valley. Play areas and short loops make it accessible without losing the mountain setting.
places.address: Gortin Glen Forest Park, Omagh, Co. Tyrone
places.parking: Free visitor car parks; scenic-drive gates may close in poor conditions.

places.name: Navan Fort
places.kicker: The ceremonial heart of ancient Ulster
places.description: Walk the great circular enclosure and climb the central mound associated with Emain Macha in Irish mythology. Exhibitions and living-history activities operate from the nearby visitor centre.
places.address: Navan Centre & Fort, Killylea Road, Armagh, BT60 4LD
places.parking: Free visitor-centre parking; check centre opening and event prices.

places.name: Gosford Forest Park
places.kicker: Woodland trails, wildlife and managed camping around Gosford Castle
places.description: Forest roads and walking loops pass arboretum trees, ponds and glimpses of the castle. A managed campsite and caravan area make this a practical overnight outdoor base rather than wild camping.
places.address: Gosford Forest Park, Markethill, Co. Armagh
places.parking: On-site parking and managed camping; check current booking and entry arrangements.

places.name: Slieve Donard
places.kicker: Northern Ireland’s highest summit above Newcastle
places.description: Climb beside the Glen River through forest before following the Mourne Wall to the 850 m summit. Sea-to-summit views are exceptional, but the upper mountain is steep and exposed.
places.address: Donard Park, Newcastle, Co. Down
places.parking: Public parking at Donard Park; arrive early on clear weekends.

places.name: Tollymore Forest Park
places.kicker: River, stone bridges and managed camping beneath the Mournes
places.description: Trails follow the Shimna River through mature forest, crossing ornate bridges and passing rocky cascades. The established campsite offers a lawful base close to Newcastle and the mountains.
places.address: Tollymore Forest Park, Bryansford, Co. Down
places.parking: Large on-site car park and bookable managed campsite; check current charges.

places.name: Tyrella Beach
places.kicker: A quiet dune-backed beach facing the Mourne Mountains
places.description: Wide sand, low dunes and a mountain skyline make Tyrella feel far removed from nearby towns. The beach is managed during the bathing season, with access arrangements varying by date.
places.address: Tyrella Beach, Downpatrick, Co. Down
places.parking: Managed beach car park; seasonal vehicle access or parking fees may apply.

places.name: Scrabo Tower
places.kicker: A landmark tower above Strangford Lough
places.description: Climb through Scrabo Country Park to the basalt hilltop and its nineteenth-century tower. The view ranges across Newtownards, the lough’s islands and the Ards Peninsula.
places.address: Scrabo Country Park, Newtownards, Co. Down
places.parking: Free car park below the tower; interior opening is limited.

places.name: Glenariff Forest Park
places.cost: Free trails · parking charge may apply
places.kicker: Waterfalls and deep woodland in the Queen of the Glens
places.description: The Waterfall Walk descends through a steep-sided glen on timber paths beside the Glenariff River. Longer forest routes climb back to open views towards the sea.
places.address: Glenariff Forest Park, Glenariff Road, Co. Antrim
places.parking: Main forest car park; check current barrier charge and opening hours.

places.name: Carrick-a-Rede
places.kicker: A rope bridge suspended above clear Atlantic water
places.description: A cliff-top path crosses flower-rich grassland to the famous bridge and views towards Rathlin Island. The coastal walk is rewarding even when bridge tickets are unavailable.
places.address: Carrick-a-Rede, Ballintoy, Co. Antrim
places.parking: National Trust parking; advance booking may be required for bridge access.

places.name: Carrickfergus Castle
places.kicker: A complete Norman fortress guarding Belfast Lough
places.description: Massive walls and a sea-facing keep tell eight centuries of military history. Walk the harbour outside for the strongest view of the castle reflected against the lough.
places.address: Marine Highway, Carrickfergus, Co. Antrim, BT38 7BG
places.parking: Public harbour parking beside the castle; check local time limits.

places.name: Benone Strand
places.cost: Free pedestrian access · vehicle charge may apply
places.kicker: A vast beach beneath Binevenagh and Mussenden Temple
places.description: One of Ireland’s longest strands runs west towards Magilligan Point, with the cliffs of Binevenagh behind and Donegal across the water. Vehicle access is managed and conditions vary with tides.
places.address: Benone Strand, Limavady, Co. Derry
places.parking: Use the managed beach and leisure-park entrances; seasonal charges may apply.

places.name: Roe Valley Country Park
places.kicker: Wooded riverside paths around historic water-powered mills
places.description: Follow the River Roe through a steep wooded valley, past rapids, footbridges and industrial remains. Several linked loops allow an easy stroll or a longer circuit.
places.address: Roe Valley Country Park, Dogleap Road, Limavady, Co. Derry
places.parking: Free car parks at the visitor centre and Dogleap Road entrances.
